problem: The sentence 'Wrap the app once in .' has lost the component name, so a student is told to wrap the app in nothing. The Provider and its store prop are never named anywhere in the chapter, yet the quiz answer later assumes the reader knows them.
fix: Wrap the app once in <Provider store={store}> from react-redux, where store is the object returned by createStore or configureStore. Every component below it can then use useSelector and useDispatch.

problem: Only the first cause in the answer is right. Two of the listed causes are wrong: a component placed outside the Provider does not show an old count, it throws a 'could not find react-redux context value' error; and a useSelector that returns a fresh object on every call causes an extra re-render (and a warning about the selector returning a different result), not a stale count.
fix: Give two real causes: (1) the reducer mutated state and returned the same object reference, so React-Redux saw no change; (2) the component copied the value once into local useState (or reads a different slice / a different store instance) instead of reading it from useSelector on each render, so it never re-reads the updated value.

problem: Redux DevTools is not middleware. It is a store enhancer, applied through the devTools option of configureStore or composeWithDevTools, so listing 'the DevTools time-travel slider' as a middleware example misclassifies it.
fix: Middleware sits between dispatch and the reducer, for example redux-thunk for async work or redux-logger for logging. The Redux DevTools time-travel slider comes from a store enhancer, not from middleware.
